long_biography.plain_text:
Alvaro Romillo Castillo has held ownership and management roles in private companies across several European jurisdictions. In Spain, he was appointed sole administrator of Linnce Software, a company formed to develop and commercialize software, databases and applications. He also held a quota in the Portuguese company Maidentok and a directorship at Cyprus-based Azesto Enterprises.

Romillo Castillo was later listed as the sole beneficial owner of the Albanian company Wortend. He was also associated with Romillo Pens, a Spanish maker of handcrafted fountain pens, where contemporary accounts connect him with its work. These activities show a pattern of direct ownership and administration, but they do not disclose reliable revenue, profit, sale proceeds or a clear chronology of personal wealth creation. Taken together, they support describing him as a private-company businessman, but not assigning a specific source or scale of wealth. Without verified economics or a durable operating focus, no one venture can be identified as the foundation of his personal wealth or as his current principal business.
